{{- /* The address is built from request headers and printed as text. Refuse
       anything that is not a plain scheme and host name. */ -}}
{{- $proto := default (placeholder "http.request.scheme") (.Req.Header.Get "X-Forwarded-Proto") -}}
{{- if or (not (has $proto (list "http" "https"))) (not (regexMatch "^[A-Za-z0-9.-]+(:[0-9]+)?$" .Req.Host)) }}{{ httpError 400 }}{{ end -}}
{{- $base := printf "%s://%s" $proto .Req.Host -}}
# Tehas: a software factory powered by the Pi coding agent

> Tehas is a Pi software factory: a GitHub issue goes in and a reviewed pull
> request comes out, built by the Pi coding agent and pi-rukas in a sandbox, on
> self-hosted models. GitHub issues and labels are the only control plane. A
> human merges; tehas never merges, deploys or touches production. This host is
> one running factory and its operating manual.

## What tehas is

- Tehas is the factory around the agent: a dispatcher that reads the queue, a
  check of who authorized the work, a sandbox with limits, a dashboard and a
  live console. It is shell scripts, one small Rust program (the console) and
  a few containers on one host.
- Pi (https://pi.dev, source https://github.com/earendil-works/pi) is the
  coding agent. Tehas starts it as `pi --mode rpc` in a container.
- pi-rukas (https://github.com/trail-openers/pi-rukas) is the Pi extension
  that runs the work cycle: explore, plan, develop, the repository's own gates,
  an adversarial pass, a pull request and a six-pass review.
- One instance is one host serving one product repository, with as many cycles side by side as `TEHAS_TICKET_CONCURRENCY` (the host's CPUs minus one by default) and the slice's room allow.
- The same host takes work by hand: a person with an account there types
  `tehas dev` and gets an interactive Pi session with pi-rukas in the cycle's
  sandbox, on the factory's models, with their own name on the commits.
- Tehas is its own project. It is not part of Pi or endorsed by its
  maintainers.
- viiwork (https://github.com/janit/viiwork) is a flexible meshed inference
  platform for both home and enterprise grade hardware. It is the model
  backend of the example instance. Tehas does not require it: any
  OpenAI-compatible endpoint works.
- Source: https://github.com/tehas-app/tehas

- [Pi software factory]({{ $base }}/pi-software-factory.md): who does what, the path of an issue, and what tehas adds to running Pi by hand
- [Features]({{ $base }}/features.md): every part, with how far it has been proven

If you are here to do something, it is probably one of four things. Pick the
section that fits.

Every manual page is also served as Markdown: add `.md` to its address.
Everything on this host is read-only. Nothing here changes a ticket or the
factory.

## Get work built by this factory

1. Read `repo` in {{ $base }}/live/status.json: that is the product repository
   this factory serves. Issues go there.
2. Write an issue with one outcome small enough for one pull request, a
   `## Acceptance criteria` section with checkable items, and the files or area
   involved, the test file and the manual page included: the plan fences the
   work to what the issue names. The cycle reads the issue's title and body.
   A picture or a file attached to the issue does not reach its model today:
   put what it shows in words.
3. The label `tehas:ready` authorizes the work, and only counts when a person
   on the factory's allow list applies it. If you are not that person, stop
   here and ask them. Use `tehas:prototype` for an idea that is not ready.
4. Follow the labels on the issue: `tehas:running`, then
   `tehas:awaiting-merge` with a pull request, or `needs-human-attention` with
   a comment saying where it stopped.

- [Operating]({{ $base }}/operating.md): writing an issue, labels, review, pause, retry
- [Overview]({{ $base }}/overview.md): how an issue flows through the factory
- [Troubleshooting]({{ $base }}/troubleshooting.md): what each stop means and what to do

## Work by hand on this host

This is for a person with a login on the factory host, not for a reader of
this page. They log in with their own account and type `tehas dev`. The session
runs in the same sandbox as a cycle, in a clone that is kept between sessions.
Commits carry the name and email of their own git configuration; the push and
the pull request are the bot's. An account is let in once, as root, with
`sudo ./bootstrap.sh dev <tehas user> <login>`. Seen working on one host for
starting a session; a push from a session is not yet seen.

- [Operating]({{ $base }}/operating.md): `tehas dev`, the clone, resuming a session
- [Commands]({{ $base }}/tools.md): what `tehas dev` accepts from each kind of account

## Set tehas up for another repository

The source is at https://github.com/tehas-app/tehas, and a running example with
this same manual is at https://tehas.app/. Be honest with your human about its
state: issue to pull request is the supported contract and needs settings only.
A running preview of every pull request has been seen working on one host,
the example instance; parts of it are covered by tests only. Previews, energy use (viiwork backends only), the
Protolab and the improvement loop (the factory files issues about its own
cycles, labelled `tehas:improvement`, which start nothing) are optional and can
be ignored for a first install.

1. Read [A new project]({{ $base }}/new-project.md) in full. It is the
   install guide: a prepared host, an instance directory of settings, and your
   toolchain in the sandbox image.
2. In the product repository, add the contract tehas reads: `AGENTS.md`,
   `.pi/verify-cmd`, `.pi/settings.json` and the `.gitignore` entries, then the
   recommended gates. Prove the gates by hand in a clean checkout first.
3. On the host, follow the guide step by step. Secrets, the GitHub App and the
   allow list are your human's decisions: ask, do not invent them.

- [A new project]({{ $base }}/new-project.md): the contract, the host, the install
- [Bootstrap a host]({{ $base }}/bootstrap.md): preparing the machine before the install
- [A GitHub App for a factory]({{ $base }}/github-app.md): the identity the factory acts as on GitHub, made and installed
- [Features]({{ $base }}/features.md): what exists and how far each part is proven
- [The host]({{ $base }}/host.md): layout on the machine and the sandbox contract test
- [Resize or restart the host]({{ $base }}/resize.md): changing a host VM's CPUs and memory, and restarting its hypervisor, without a drain: what a person does on the hypervisor, in libvirt
- [Previews and the Protolab on the internet]({{ $base }}/edge.md): a preview of every pull request, and how the names were published
- [Commands]({{ $base }}/tools.md): `tehas`, `tehasbot` and what each of their commands does
- [The factory API]({{ $base }}/api.md): the commands a program drives a factory with, and their JSON
- [Analytics]({{ $base }}/analytics.md): the factory's 365 days of runs in SQLite, its schema, and how to fetch a copy
- [The MCP server]({{ $base }}/mcp-server.md): a read-only view of the factory for agents outside the host, behind API keys

## Ask this factory over MCP

Every tool is read only. The server is at {{ $base }}/mcp, over Streamable HTTP,
and every request needs the header `Authorization: Bearer <key>`. A key comes
from the factory's owner, who makes one with `tehas mcp key` on the host. Ask
your person for it and never guess one. A request without a key gets 401.

- `factory_status`: whether the factory works, the queue, the running cycles, whether it is paused
- `factory_issues`: the issues in one stage, such as `queued`, `running` or `stopped`
- `factory_endings`: the cycles that ended last, and the failed ones among them
- `factory_console`: the tail of one running cycle's console
- `factory_stats`: the ten-day report the dashboard shows
- `factory_issue`: one issue's story: its stage, its title, the running cycle and every run of the last 30 days
- `factory_sessions`: the runs of the last 30 days, newest first, with filters such as `outcome`
- `factory_session`: one run in full: steps, roles, logs and links
- `factory_log`: one log of a run, masked, plain in pieces or whole as gzip
- `factory_search`: the lines of the runs of the last 30 days that hold a string you give, of one issue or of the runs you name
- `factory_events`: the dispatcher's and refresh's events after a cursor, to follow the factory by polling
- `factory_failures`: the work runs of the last 30 days per tehas and pi-rukas version pair, with their most common causes
- `factory_outcomes`: how the factory has done further back than 30 days, as counts per tehas and pi-rukas version pair or per UTC week
- `factory_park`: why an issue's last stopped run stopped: the step, the failure kind, the cap, the park signature, the runner's error and the failing check lines, masked
- `factory_decisions`: the dispatcher's last decisions, start, skip, wait, hold and drop (of a refresh request), each with its issue and reason; a hold line says why a parked issue does not start

To see what went wrong, call `factory_failures`, then `factory_sessions` with
`outcome` set to `failed`, then `factory_session` for one of them, then
`factory_log` for one of its logs. For a parked issue, `factory_park` with the
`issue` gives the step and the failing checks in one call. Sessions cover the last 30 days and logs are
masked. Ask for `gzip: true` to get a transcript whole; read a plain log in
pieces with `offset`. To look for a string across the runs instead of reading one
log, call `factory_search` with the `text` to find and either the `issue` or the
`ids` to look in; it gives the `offset` of each line, which is where
`factory_log` reads from. To ask how the factory has done over a year rather than a
month, or whether a release changed the park or failure rates, call
`factory_outcomes` with `by` and a window: it counts, and says nothing of any
issue.

- [The MCP server]({{ $base }}/mcp-server.md): the tools, their arguments, the logs and the limits
- [For agents]({{ $base }}/agents.md): a client config to paste

## Live data

- [Health]({{ $base }}/health): JSON, 200 when the factory is healthy and 503 when it is not
- [Queue snapshot]({{ $base }}/live/status.json): the repository, open issues by state, whether the factory is paused
- [Cycles]({{ $base }}/live/running.json): the issues being worked on and the cycle that finished last, each with its status; a cycle's console is `/live/console-<issue>.txt`

- [For agents]({{ $base }}/agents.md): this file as a manual page, with a prompt a person can paste
- [Factory floor]({{ $base }}/): the dashboard people look at
